subject: Atlas Health — serving mode check and migration origin
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@atlashealth.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up and next steps after today’s POC kickoff

Hi Emily / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time today. Good alignment overall. To make sure we capture the right technical path for the POC, a couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) Current serving origin: you mentioned most of the request traffic today comes through OpenAI’s API with a small percentage hitting a self-hosted cluster for latency-sensitive flows — can you confirm which of your services (claims routing / triage / summarization) are on the self-hosted cluster today?

2) Target deployment preference: you listed three options that might work for Atlas Health: Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), or Private VPC. For the POC, what matters most: lowest latency, strict data residency, or cost predictability? Please rank 1–3.

3) Migration constraints: any procurement or legal gating we should anticipate if we propose a Dedicated or Private option (e.g., vendor-side MFAs, vendor onboarding questionnaire timelines, required SLA language)?

Attached is a lightweight mutual action plan draft and a short migration checklist. If you’re comfortable, can you fill in the priority ranking and share any internal constraints? We’ll use that to propose a POC configuration (hardware/quantization, routing policy, and fallback plan).

Next suggested steps (proposed):
- You: confirm service mapping & priorities by EOD Wednesday (2026-11-04)
- Us: produce two POC configs (Hosted-focused and Dedicated-focused) and a rough SOW estimate by 2026-11-06
- Quick tech sync (30 min) week of 2026-11-09 to align scope

Thanks — we’ll be ready to move fast once we have your constraints.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v2.xlsx (12KB)]

From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@atlashealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps after today’s POC kickoff

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below and I added a couple of constraints.

1) Serving origin: our triage service (triage.atlashealth.com) and the claims-summarizer (summaries service) are currently on the self-hosted GPU pool (NVIDIA A100s) — approximately 30% of inference volume. The rest (~70%) is routed to OpenAI via our API gateway.

2) Priority ranking for the POC: 
   1. Latency for triage endpoints (real-time routing decisions)
   2. Data residency/compliance for PHI-adjacent data (must remain in our VPC or a provider-managed VPC in us-west)
   3. Cost predictability (important but secondary for the first POC)

3) Procurement / legal: we have a standard vendor security review that typically takes 2–3 weeks once we have SOC 2 docs and an IP/data processing addendum. Our procurement rep also needs estimated monthly committed spend if we evaluate Dedicated.

We reviewed the mutual action plan and made a few inline comments — sending back the version shortly. Attached is our migration-notes.csv that shows the current split by service (small file).

Can we push the tech sync to 2026-11-10? Rajesh and I are out 11/9.

Best,
Emily
Director of Platform Engineering | Atlas Health
emily.hart@atlashealth.com
[Attachment: migration-checklist.csv (3KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@atlashealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps after today’s POC kickoff

Emily — great context, thank you. A couple quick notes from the commercial side so we can prepare useful numbers for procurement: 

- For Dedicated we’ll provide an estimated committed monthly price band based on expected token and p90 latency targets. If latency is the top priority for triage, Dedicated or Private will likely be the best fit since it avoids multi-tenant scheduling variability.
- For Private VPC we’ll need to confirm the network peering and KMS requirements (HSM vs customer-managed key) — if you have a security contact we should loop in now, it speeds the SOC2 + onboarding.
- We’ll include a simple TCO comparison in the POC SOW (hosted vs dedicated vs private) that reflects expected token volumes from your migration CSV.

Logan / Aditya — I’d like the Hosted-focused and Dedicated-focused POC configs to both include a routing fallback to the OpenAI endpoint for non-critical flows and a KV-prefix cache for summaries to reduce token costs — please include that in the configs.

Emily — we can do the tech sync 2026-11-10 at 10:00am PT if that works for your team. I’ll send a calendar invite after Logan shares the POC config timeline.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (98KB), mutual_action_plan_v2.xlsx (updated, 16KB)]

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Emily Hart <emily.hart@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up and next steps after today’s POC kickoff

Thanks — quick confirmation from our side before the tech sync: 

- We can commit a 3-month Dedicated trial window if the latency numbers meet our p95/p99 targets; procurement will still want a monthly committed estimate but is willing to treat the trial as a scoped pilot.
- Security / KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys in a VPC for PHI-adjacent traffic. If Redwood supports a hybrid pattern (private VPC for triage + Hosted for lower-risk bulk processing) that would be ideal.
- Please flag any items in the mutual action plan that require sign-off from our legal team vs procurement vs engineering.

See you on 11/10.

—
Rajesh Patel
Head of Infrastructure | Atlas Health
rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com
